metadata.role: 70 reference-annotated lines (50 H1 + 20 H2) for final -e and syllable-count agreement
metadata.edition: W. W. Skeat (ed.), The Complete Works of Geoffrey Chaucer, vol. 4, The Canterbury Tales: Text, 2nd ed., Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1900 (Project Gutenberg #22120).

lines.text: Whan that Aprille with his shoures sote

final_e_decisions.reason: Skeat spells Aprille with sounded -e before consonant (or headless if apocopated)

lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: The droghte of Marche hath perced to the rote,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And bathed every veyne in swich licour,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Of which vertu engendred is the flour;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Whan Zephirus eek with his swete breeth
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Inspired hath in every holt and heeth
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: The tendre croppes, and the yonge sonne
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Hath in the Ram his halfe cours y-ronne,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And smale fowles maken melodye,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That slepen al the night with open yë,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: (So priketh hem nature in hir corages):
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Than longen folk to goon on pilgrimages
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: (And palmers for to seken straunge strondes)
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: To ferne halwes, couthe in sondry londes;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And specially, from every shires ende
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Of Engelond, to Caunterbury they wende,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: The holy blisful martir for to seke,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That hem hath holpen, whan that they were seke.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Bifel that, in that seson on a day,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: In Southwerk at the Tabard as I lay
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Redy to wenden on my pilgrimage
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: To Caunterbury with ful devout corage,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: At night was come in-to that hostelrye
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Wel nyne and twenty in a companye,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Of sondry folk, by aventure y-falle
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: In felawshipe, and pilgrims were they alle,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That toward Caunterbury wolden ryde;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: The chambres and the stables weren wyde,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And wel we weren esed atte beste.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And shortly, whan the sonne was to reste,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: So hadde I spoken with hem everichon,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That I was of hir felawshipe anon,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And made forward erly for to ryse,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: To take our wey, ther as I yow devyse.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: But natheles, whyl I have tyme and space,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Er that I ferther in this tale pace,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Me thinketh it acordaunt to resoun,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: To telle yow al the condicioun
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Of ech of hem, so as it semed me,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And whiche they weren, and of what degree;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And eek in what array that they were inne:
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And at a knight than wol I first biginne.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: A KNIGHT ther was, and that a worthy man,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That fro the tyme that he first bigan
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: To ryden out, he loved chivalrye,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Trouthe and honour, fredom and curteisye.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Ful worthy was he in his lordes werre,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And therto hadde he riden (no man ferre)
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: As wel in Cristendom as hethenesse,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And ever honoured for his worthinesse.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Doun at the rote of Vesulus the colde,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: A lusty playne, habundant of vitaille,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Wher many a tour and toun thou mayst biholde,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: That founded were in tyme of fadres olde,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And many another delitable sighte,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And Saluces this noble contree highte.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: A markis whylom lord was of that londe,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: As were his worthy eldres him bifore;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And obeisant and redy to his honde
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Were alle his liges, bothe lasse and more.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Thus in delyt he liveth, and hath don yore,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Biloved and drad, thurgh favour of fortune,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Bothe of his lordes and of his commune.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Therwith he was, to speke as of linage,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: The gentilleste y-born of Lumbardye,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: A fair persone, and strong, and yong of age,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And ful of honour and of curteisye;
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Discreet y-nogh his contree for to gye,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: Save in somme thinges that he was to blame,
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.

lines.text: And Walter was this yonge lordes name.
lines.commentary_source: L. D. Benson (ed.), The Riverside Chaucer, 3rd ed., pp. xlii-xlv; Harvard Geoffrey Chaucer Website, Lesson 2; W. W. Skeat (1900), vol. 5 notes.
